The note is mistaken: in philosophy, Austin (J. L. Austin) is called a "naive empiricist" because his account of knowledge treats ordinary sensory observation as a straightforward, reliable foundation, allegedly overlooking skeptical doubts, theory-laden perception, and the inferential work needed to justify empirical claims. The label is a criticism of his epistemology, not of any account of law or legal systems.

CONFIDENCE: 55
